About me
Bengaluru, India
Mission

Turn ideas into deployed AI products — grounding LLM agents in real data with RAG so they never hallucinate, and shipping models that teams can actually use.

Vision

Become the engineer teams trust to take an AI idea from a notebook to a live, production-ready application.

I'm a Computer Science graduate (2025) who builds AI products end to end — from a Google Gemini-powered RAG agent to a classical ML pipeline — and ships every one of them as a live, working app.

My core is data science: I work across GenAI, machine learning, NLP, and business intelligence rather than staying in one lane. In GenAI, I build LLM agents with the Google Gemini API, grounding every answer in structured data and policy documents through RAG so responses can't drift into hallucination, and enforcing role-based access control at the data layer rather than the prompt layer. Alongside that, I work across classical ML — multi-classifier pipelines (Logistic Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost, SVM), GridSearchCV-tuned models, and imbalanced-data handling with SMOTE — and NLP, using Hugging Face Transformers, zero-shot classification (BART MNLI), and Sentence Transformers for semantic search.

I work primarily in Python — Scikit-learn, TensorFlow, Keras, Pandas — backed by SQL/NoSQL data modeling in MySQL, PostgreSQL, and MongoDB, and I deploy everything on Streamlit Cloud so the work is something people can actually click into, not just a notebook. I also build BI dashboards in Tableau, most recently one modeling 99K+ orders and $16M+ in revenue — the same data science instincts (EDA, hypothesis testing, clean data pipelines) that underpin the ML and GenAI work.

My foundation is a B.Tech in Computer Science from Jain College of Engineering & Technology, with coursework spanning machine learning, databases, operating systems, and software engineering. What stands out across my three internships and nine projects is a habit: I don't ship a model or agent without quantifying it first — accuracy, F1, ROC-AUC — and without a live demo a non-technical stakeholder can actually try.
